messages:
alice: FYI the canary for gpu-serving-stack failed during the pipeline run, blocking the whole rollout. helm pre-install hook errored when trying to materialize env secrets from sops keys.
ben: link to the pipeline?
alice: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/9853/builds/412 — error excerpt below.
alice: ```
Error: pre-install hook "sync-env-hook" failed: command terminated with exit code 1
stderr: open /var/run/secrets/env-symlink: permission denied
stdout: attempting to decrypt with sops key id: 7a3f-...
```
carmen: interesting — we rotated the sops key last night in k8s-keys, but the sealed-secrets controller in eu-west is still on the old keyset version. Can we confirm key aliasing?
dana: I saw the k8s-keys rotation job succeed but the helm chart uses a prehook that expects the decrypted file at init time. If the sealed secret can't be decrypted the hook just fails.
infra-oncall: deploy-bot reported "sealed-secrets: key id mismatch" on 04:12UTC in eu-west-1. I restarted sealed-secrets controller pod, it came up but logs show 'no matching key for sops ID 7a3f' repeatedly.
ben: do we keep previous key material in KMS/HSM? The rotation job should have kept the previous key unwrapped for 7 days.
carmen: yes, previous key material retained, but the sealed-secret objects were re-created during the noise-reconciliation and now reference the new annotation that the controller doesn't accept. Looks like helm upgrade created new sealed secrets before controller finished loading the new key.
dana: quick mitigation: disable the pre-install hook for the canary job and re-run the pipeline so the pod can come up and we can triage without gating critical traffic. Also consider temporarily pinning to the older sealed-secret annotation.
alice: can we avoid disabling hook in prod — I want to avoid secrets-on-disk drift. Alternative: have the hook fall back to reading from env directly if symlink creation fails. That would make rollout more robust.
ben: For immediate recovery, I toggled the canary pipeline to skip the hook (CI override flag) and kicked a manual deploy. Can confirm the canary pods started but some components logged decrypt failures on startup (they retry).
infra-oncall: action items: 1) roll sealed-secrets controller to pick up rotated key (in progress), 2) revert helm chart change that re-created sealedsecret objects (PR #1208 revert queued), 3) add a post-rotate job to reconcile hook annotations across clusters.
carmen: I'm adding a short-term helm chart change: hook becomes idempotent and tolerates 'permission denied' by falling back to in-cluster env var lookup. Will open PR with minimal change.
dana: long-term: update CI pipeline to 1) wait for sealed-secrets controller readiness after key rotation, 2) run a canary decrypt check step that uses sopsctl to decrypt target sealed secret before helm apply, 3) mark rotate events with a circuit that prevents simultaneous sealedsecret re-creation.
ben: log snippets from sealed-secrets controller to help root cause: ```
I0315 04:11:02.123 controller.go:237] No key matching sops id 7a3f found, skipping
I0315 04:11:05.456 controller.go:245] Loaded key set v2 from kms alias projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/sops/cryptoKeys/sops-v2
I0315 04:11:05.457 controller.go:248] keys mismatch: object annotated with key v1, controller has v2 only
```
alice: good detective work. Please also add an incident note in #incidents about the cross-region rollout constraint — we should document that sops key rotations are a global event and need staged rollout.
dana: done. I've filed an infra ticket RFC to standardize a rotation checklist and updated the Cost/Deployment playbook to recommend a 30m stabilization window after key ops. Ticket: INF-938.
infra-oncall: closing loop: canary is stable after manual override and controller rotation. We'll keep the revert PR queued until chart fallback is merged. If anyone sees lingering decrypt errors, ping me and I'll force a controller restart in the region. :thumbsup:
